planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants after last frost in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; its low, dense habit suits border edges and container growing as well as the herb bed.

directions: Plant in lean, well-drained soil in full sun, where the plant develops its strongest flavor. Compactum is a dwarf oregano selection that stays low and dense, only 4–8 inches tall, forming a tidy mound rather than the looser, more upright growth of standard oregano, making it useful as a fragrant edging plant or rock garden filler in addition to a culinary herb. It carries the same bold, aromatic flavor as standard oregano in a more compact package suited to smaller herb gardens and containers. Harvest sprigs regularly and shear plants back after flowering to keep growth dense and productive for years.

common_name: The Blues Little Bluestem (Fine-Textured Powder-Blue Native Grass)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, lean soil in full sun; like other little bluestem selections, The Blues performs poorly in rich, overfed soil.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; little bluestem thrives in poor, rocky, clay, or sandy soil and performs poorly if overfed. The Blues produces exceptionally fine-textured, powder-blue foliage through summer, among the most intensely blue of the little bluestem cultivars, turning warm copper-orange in fall with fluffy silvery seed heads that catch low autumn and winter light beautifully. Its upright, airy habit and strong color make it a striking textural contrast against darker-foliaged perennials and shrubs in a naturalistic border or meadow planting. It is extremely drought-tolerant once established and provides valuable seed and cover for birds; cut back to a few inches in late winter before new growth begins.

common_name: Pink Chintz Thyme (Fuzzy Gray-Green Creeping Thyme)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container-grown plants in spring or fall in very well-drained, sandy or gritty, lean soil in full sun; thyme rots readily in wet, heavy soil.

directions: Plant in full sun in very well-drained, sandy or gritty, lean soil; thyme rots quickly in wet or heavy ground. Pink Chintz is a low, mat-forming creeping thyme with soft, fuzzy, gray-green leaves that give the foliage a distinctive downy texture, covered in a heavy flush of small salmon-pink flowers in late spring to early summer that draw bees in large numbers. Its dense, mat-forming habit makes it a favorite for planting between stepping stones and pavers, where light foot traffic releases its herbal fragrance, as well as for draping over rock walls and border edges. Shear lightly after flowering to keep the mat tidy and encourage dense new growth.

common_name: John Creech Sedum (Compact Scalloped-Leaf Groundcover Stonecrop)

planting.note: Plant cuttings or divisions in spring in very well-drained, dry to average, rocky or sandy, lean soil in full sun to partial shade.

directions: Plant cuttings or divisions in spring in very well-drained, dry to average, lean, rocky or sandy soil in full sun to partial shade. John Creech is a compact, tidy selection of Caucasian stonecrop, staying lower and more restrained than the vigorous straight species, forming a dense mat of small, scalloped, bright green leaves topped by clusters of star-shaped pink flowers in midsummer. Its smaller scale and less aggressive spread make it a better fit for rock gardens, container plantings, and small-space groundcover than more rampant sedum spurium cultivars, while still spreading readily enough to fill in bare, dry spots quickly. Extremely low-maintenance and drought-tolerant once established; propagate easily from stem cuttings that root at the leaf nodes.
